classification.difficultyReason: Apply the vertical line test directly to four supplied graphs without calculation.

content.prompt: Determine whether the following graphs represent functions or relations.

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, printed questions 2–5, upper-left graph.
spec.description: An unscaled cubic-shaped blue curve crosses the origin, has a local maximum to the right of the vertical axis, crosses the positive horizontal axis, has a local minimum below it, then crosses that axis again. Both curve ends have arrowheads. Black axes have positive-end arrowheads and x and y labels.
spec.mathematics: One output for each horizontal coordinate. Preserve the two turning points and three horizontal-axis crossings. Bézier coordinates are unlabelled drawing coordinates; no equation, numerical scale or turning-point values are asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied graph remains visible in the question. Classification and vertical-line-test reasoning appear only in the answer.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects the graph at most once. A function is also a relation.

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, printed questions 2–5, upper-right graph.
spec.description: A blue right-opening sideways parabola has its vertex at the axes' intersection. Its upper and lower branches are symmetric about the horizontal axis and carry outward arrowheads. Black axes have positive-end arrowheads and x and y labels.
spec.mathematics: The two branches give two outputs for positive horizontal coordinates. Internal drawing coordinates establish the unscaled shape only; no equation or numerical values are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied graph remains visible in the question. No test line or classification is added to the question diagram.

answer.worked: Not a function: a vertical line to the right of the origin intersects both branches. This relation has two outputs for some inputs.

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, printed questions 2–5, lower-left graph.
spec.description: An unfilled blue circle is centred at the intersection of black perpendicular axes. Both axes extend beyond the circle and have positive-end arrowheads and x and y labels. There is no centre dot, radius, numerical tick or equation.
spec.mathematics: Preserve a true circle, equal physical coordinate units and two intersections with each axis. The internal drawing radius is not a supplied mathematical measurement.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied circle and axes remain visible in the question. Classification and intersection reasoning are answer-only.

answer.worked: Not a function: the $y$-axis intersects the circle twice. This relation has two outputs for some inputs.

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, printed questions 2–5, lower-right graph.
spec.description: An increasing, concave-up blue exponential-shaped curve remains above the horizontal axis. Its left tail approaches that axis from above and has a leftward arrowhead; its right tail rises steeply with an upward arrowhead. Black axes have positive-end arrows and x and y labels. The positive vertical-axis intercept is unlabelled.
spec.mathematics: Preserve the single-valued increasing shape, concavity and approach to the horizontal axis. Bézier coordinates specify the unscaled drawing only; no exponential equation or intercept value is inferred.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied graph remains visible in the question. The classification and its reason appear only in the answer.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects the graph at most once. A function is also a relation.
